ch34.d.f: Size of the focal length $\lvert f \rvert$
ch34.d.p: Distance $p$ from the object to the lens or mirror; dragging the tip of the object also changes it
ch34.d.h: Height of the object arrow; drag its tip up or down
ch34.l.goal.rays: Three principal rays from the tip of the object pass the lens and meet at the tip of the image
ch34.l.goal.sign: If the rays really meet, the image is real ($i > 0$, beyond the lens); if only their extensions meet, it is virtual ($i < 0$, on the object side)
ch34.l.obs.drag: Rays: green parallel to the axis, then through $F_2$; pink straight through the centre; orange through $F_1$, then parallel to the axis
ch34.l.obs.2f: Converging lens, object beyond $2f$: smaller, inverted, real image. At $p = 2f$ the same size ($m = -1$)
ch34.l.obs.f: Drag the object toward the focal point: the image moves away and grows; at $p = f$ the rays leave parallel and the image is at infinity
ch34.l.obs.inside: Inside the focal point ($p < f$): the rays spread, their extensions (dashed) meet on the object side, giving an enlarged, upright, virtual image (a magnifier)
ch34.l.obs.div: Diverging lens: a smaller, upright, virtual image wherever the object is
ch34.m.goal.rays: Three principal rays from the tip of the object reflect from the mirror and meet at the tip of the image
ch34.m.goal.sign: If they meet in front of the mirror (object side) the image is real ($i > 0$); if only their extensions meet behind it, virtual ($i < 0$)
ch34.m.obs.drag: Rays: green parallel to the axis, then through $F$; pink to the centre of the mirror, reflected symmetrically; orange through $F$, then parallel to the axis
ch34.m.obs.inside: Concave mirror, inside the focal point ($p < f$): enlarged, upright, virtual image (a make-up mirror)
ch34.m.obs.convex: Convex mirror: always a smaller, upright, virtual image and a wide field of view (a car side mirror)
ch34.m.obs.plane: Plane mirror: $i = -p$ and $m = 1$, a same-size virtual image as far behind the mirror as the object is in front
ch34.assume.thin: Paraxial approximation: rays stay close to the axis at small angles. Lenses and mirrors are treated as thin elements that refract or reflect in one plane; the mirror's curvature is only drawn
ch34.l.assume.sign: Signs: converging lens $f > 0$, diverging lens $f < 0$, real image $i > 0$, virtual image $i < 0$
ch34.m.assume.sign: Signs: concave mirror $f > 0$, convex mirror $f < 0$, plane mirror $f = \infty$, real image $i > 0$, virtual image $i < 0$
